name: Essential Artificial
summary: In Ironforge, Essential Artificial parts remain vital to gnomish tinkers and engineers rebuilding from exile. Stockpiles were left behind when the gnomes fled Gnomeregan.

sections.title: Standard Issue Ingenuity
sections.body: Before Gnomeregan fell, tinkers called the Essential Artificial a nigh-universal component. Gnomish engineers fitted it into countless contraptions, clockwork wonders, and heavy machinery throughout the subterranean halls. Its standardized design gave smiths and machinists reliable parts they could interchange.

sections.title: Salvage from the Depths
sections.body: The trogg invasion and radiation disaster drove the gnomes from Gnomeregan in a desperate rush. Large reserves of Essential Artificial parts stayed behind in heavy, steam-powered dispensers called artificial extrapolators, scattered through the deeper passages. In Tinker Town, master craftsman Klockmort Spannerspan actively recruits daring adventurers to return to the contaminated ruins and salvage the parts, so research and invention can continue.

faq.answer: An Essential Artificial is a standardized, versatile mechanical component that gnomish smiths and tinkers use in experiments, machines, and contraptions.

faq.q: Why were they left behind in Gnomeregan?
faq.answer: The trogg invasion and deadly radiation forced the gnomes to flee in a rush, leaving stockpiles of everyday components in storage devices.
Ambitious inventor Klockmort Spannerspan, based in Tinker Town within Ironforge, seeks the parts for his ongoing experiments and technological research in exile.

faq.q: Where are they found inside the ruins?
aliases: where do i find essential artificials
faq.answer: Essential Artificial parts are stored in large, steam-powered containers called artificial extrapolators throughout the deeper levels of contaminated Gnomeregan.

angles.text: As a gnome, recovering each component from Gnomeregan's irradiated corridors helps your people rebuild their technological superiority while taking refuge in Ironforge.
As an engineer, you can appreciate how these nigh-universal parts fit seamlessly into varied machinery and experimental designs.
